findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee begin to don gloves without handwashing. CORRECTED- the employee was interrupted and directed to wash hands. The employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Inspector provided education and demonstrated correct hand washing, which the employee modeled afterwards (rinse hands, scrub with soap, dry with paper towel and use barrier to turn off to avoid recontaminating hands). Review hand washing procedures and times to wash with all employees who serve or handle food. Inspector provided a handout regarding times to wash hands. Times to wash hands include but are not limited to: before donning gloves, after using using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, etc.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken stored over ready to eat (RTE) cooked and peeled eggs in the standing cooler. CORRECTED- chicken was moved below the eggs. Ensure all animals proteins are stored to reflect increasing internal cooking temperatures (top-> bottom= RTE foods, unwashed produce, washed produce, raw eggs/ shellfish/ seafood, pork, and chicken) to prevent the cross contamination of foods. Inspector provided a handout to the PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple sink to be set up in the following format: wash-sanitize-rinse. CORRECTED- the sink was remade to reflect proper ware washing: (wash- rinse-sanitize), and a handout was provided to the PIC. Rinsing after sanitizing prevents proper contact time between the sanitizer and food contact surface. Ensure the triple sink is always made to reflect proper ware washing moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(A) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (A) Hot water manual operations by immersion for at least 30 seconds and as specified under § 4-501.111.[P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed cooked rice holding an internal temperature of 114F. CORRECTED- the item was moved under TIME AS CONTROL (TAC)- the item was stated to have been prepared at 11 AM, and will be used or discarded by 3PM. Once rice (or noodles, or vegetables) are cooked they become temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods- and therefore must be held below 41F or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Ensure all TCS foods are kept outside of the temperature danger zone.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple sauces labeled “refrigerate after opening” held on the counter. Sauces included garlic Parmesan and garlic buffalo sauce. CORRECTED- The PIC stated the bottles were just opened and items were moved to cold holding. Ensure all TCS foods are cold held below 41F or hot held above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The steam table in the kitchen- that is the only piece of equipment that is used for hot holding was observed to not be functioning. The PIC stated that there is an electrical issue with the outlets that is causing issues with the equipment. Disposable votive burners that are typically used for short-term hot holding are being used under foil pans. These burners are allowing the food items hot holding to maintain temperatures of 135F and above for the time being. This is not a long term solution and the steam table either needs to be repaired or another method of hot holding needs to be obtained. A follow up is scheduled for 5/20/2026 to ensure the steam table is functional or another method of hot holding has been obtained.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw fish in reduced oxygen packaging thawing in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding thawing in reduced oxygen packaging, and packages were cut to be vented. Ensure items in reduced oxygen packaging are vented or removed from packaging when thawing to prevent the growth of anaerobic bacteria such as Clostridium botulinum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plates being stored at the server station with the food contact surface facing upwards, and silverware stored with the food contact surface outwards. CORRECTED- the plates were flipped and the silverware was inverted. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects against bare hand contamination and contamination from the environment.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The PIC stated they no longer had sanitizing test strips since the dish machine was removed. The facility uses bleach for chemical sanitation at the triple sink, and quaternary ammonia for sanitizer in the bottle used for food contact surfaces. The inspector will return for a follow up inspection on 5/20/26 to ensure test strips have been obtained. Ensure a test kit (for BOTH chlorine bleach and quaternary ammonia) is available to verify proper sanitizing concentrations of chemicals used to sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed used water in the basin of a mop bucket in the back of the kitchen. CORRECTED- the mop water was dumped. Mops absorb fats, oils, and grease. Ensure mop water (once used- classified as waste water) is dumped immediately after use moving forward.
* This violation was previously noted as violation #55
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: There is a bare wood table surface in the wait area just below the pass-thru window. Paint or otherwise seal the bare wood surface so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Dirty mop water was observed in a mop bucket in the kitchen. PIC indicated that the mop water was from the previous day. Ensure that water is disposed immediately after mopping and that the mop bucket is stored empty.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: A piece of trim tile is missing along the wall into the cookline. Replace the trim tile.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed staff not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing activity. Discussed with owner during the inspection. Be vigilant with food handling and create a policy to insure staff understands proper hand washing. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12:  Observed the hand sink to not be supplied with soap and paper towel. The soap and paper towels were provided during the inspection, however, they were pulled from locations near the cookline and dish machine. Owner discussed providing a permanent fixture for the soap and paper towels to keep them from moving around the kitchen. 

Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11:  Observed fish to be stored beneath chicken in the refrigerator adjacent to the cookline. Corrected during the inspection. Discussed storage order with owners and staff. See that staff is educated on proper storage order as part of their onboarding experience. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13:  The interior and exterior of the while upright cooler of the cookline is observed coated with crumbs and splash. See that the refrigerator is maintained clean. Discussed creating a cleaning schedule and seeing the staff is completely daily tasks to maintain a clean kitchen. Cleaning once a week has proven insufficient. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: The owner continues to have a number of operations being improperly conducted. Today there is no bleach in the facility nor any sanitizing solution for the dish machine. Owner is failing to properly monitor temperatures, thawing, bleach, and dish machine operations. Today the facility was not particularly busy and the kitchen is still in disarray. Educate staff so they are able to support safe food handling practices. Come into the store and close each night so you are set-up for success: have paper towel, bleach buckets, soap, and stem thermometer available. 
Creating a follow-up for a later date to allow time for operator to educate staff and create proper procedures that allow for safe food handling. 


Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: There are no employee health papers available. Provide signed reporting agreements and see that staff is educated on when to call-off sick from work. 
Follow-up is being completed at a later date to allow operator to establish safe food handling practices and create binders holding required paperwork so they are readily available for the inspector. 

(O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: There is no paperwork available at the facility. See that a binder is created to hold all required paper work. Binder should be readily available for inspection. EDUCATE staff on procedures for disposal of vomit and diarrhea. 

A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There is a hole in the HVAC duct work over the reach-in freezer that is creating a drip. The drips are falling directly onto the surface of the reach-in freezer AND any foods being prepped on that unit. See that the reach-in freezer is not used as a food preparation area as there is potential for cross-contamination. There was a batter being prepared atop the reach-in freezer during the inspection. It was moved as the droplets of condensation were observed forming over the food. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Raw eggs are observed being stored over fresh fruit and waffles. The waffles and fruits were moved during the inspection. A storage order sign was provided to owner. See that storage labels are created for the shelving so staff knows where to place various foods. Personal foods and beverages should be stored on the lowest shelf. Continue to educate staff on proper storage order. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There is observed bags of chicken intermixed with a bag of fish in the triple sink. Discussed proper storage and cooking temperatures. The chicken cooks at a higher temperature to destroy Salmonella. See that chicken is thawed separately from pork, beef, and fish. Bag of catfish was moved during the inspection into the walk-in cooler. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: There is no bleach available for the creation of sani-buckets. Owner was asked to call for bleach during the inspection and inspectors will not leave until bleach is available. Keep Chlorox or any USEPA registered bleach available in-house. Nothing the whitens, brightens, deodorizes, scented, or splashless should be used. There is a splashless bleach available and a disinfectant available. The disinfectant’s label reads that the product is only to be used on non-porous, non-food contact surfaces.  

(D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: The facility has an empty sanitizing bucket attached to their dish machine. No sanitizer is available. The facility may not use the dish machine until proper chemical is provided. The dish machine should be monitored daily: every morning, between lulls in use, and between the switching of buckets. TEST, TEST, TEST to monitor. Sanitizing is one of the most critical steps in your safe food handling operations. The triple sink is being used throughout the day to support facility operations (thawing and food preparation). Without proper sanitizing, you are not reducing pathogens present from customer-to-customer and between raw proteins and ready-to-eat foods. 
The facility is going to get chemical from GFS. Do not use the dish machine until chemical is provided and TESTED within dish machine. 

After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Chicken is observed thawing in a tub of water on the preparation counter. The chicken was almost through the thawing process and was becoming ambient temperature. Proper thawing practices were discussed. PLAN AHEAD and place frozen foods in the walk-in cooler days before needed. The walk-in cooler has space for additional shelving. This may be needed to support the growing business. Bakers racks are tall and have five or six shelves. More storage would support thawing. Chicken was returned to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. 
Also, a large number of shrimp are observed being stored on the preparation counter during lunch and then dinner. The food is returned to the walk-in cooler but this is an example of temperature abuse - the food is repeatedly moved through warm and then cooled practices. Think about portioning the shrimp prior to storage so you can grab a few bags during busy periods. OR simply bring less shrimp out of the cooler during busy periods. 
Shrimp was returned to cooler during the inspection. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: The facility is observed improperly thawing chicken and fish. Frozen bags were observed in the triple sink with no water running. The fish was moved to the walk-in cooler and the chicken was placed under running water. 

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: The facility is in the habit of storing in-use utensils atop the foods on the steam table. These utensils will grow bacteria in-between uses and will introduce bacteria into foods if not properly handled. See that utensils are removed for wash, rinse, and sanitizing between busy periods - less than four hours between removal. Discussed the use of metal versus plastic utensils. The metal is preferred as it is sturdy. But the metal handle quickly becomes heated. See that appropriate time management is used with these utensils. 
(A) UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Facility had multiple priority and priority foundation violations, including lack of knowledge regarding employee health, lack of handwashing before donning gloves, inadequate storage to prevent cross contamination, and a lack of sanitizer within the facility. 
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items. [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Food employees were not fully aware of symptoms that would prevent them from working around food and could not name specific symptoms or diagnoses. Review employee reporting agreements with all employees and keep signed agreements on file for review during health inspections.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Two employee beverages were observed on the prep counter without lids or straws. CORRECTED- Employee beverages were discarded. Ensure employee drinks are in containers with a lid and straw, otherwise store employee beverages in a separate area and ensure employees wash hands before returning to handling food/dishes/clean utensils/etc.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employees were observed returning to the kitchen, donning gloves, and moving between dirty and clean dishes without washing hands. Handwashing is required before donning gloves, before moving from dirty to clean dishes, and upon returning to the kitchen. Changing gloves does not replace handwashing. Discussed handwashing with PIC. Review handwashing (when to wash and procedure) with employees.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No soap or paper towels were available at the handsink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Soap and paper towels were provided upon request. Ensure soap and paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1) Raw meats and fish were stored above fruits, lettuce, and rice in the walk-in cooler. 2) Raw fish was stored below raw chicken in the cookline fridge. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage to prevent cross contamination. Store raw meats below produce. Store Raw chicken below fish.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
One spray bottle containing pink liquid was observed unlabeled in the kitchen. Two spray bottles in the bar area were observed without labels. Ensure all chemicals are labeled to indicate contents. CORRECTED- Bottles were labeled.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Facility did not have any sanitizer prepared or available during this inspection. Ensure sanitizer is always available and prepared during times of food prep and service. PIC sent an employee to purchase more sanitizer during the inspection.
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. [Pf]
